content.comment_body: Hello [user_name]. As of January 2023, I am unable to get my [product_name] project functional. The PLC is running and AWS shows it is reachable. The project loads to AWS, I get the [url] and the page opens. However, none of the controls work and there is no data exchange. I attempted different AWS regions since I am in Mexico, and also tried your suggested workaround. Did I promise too much to my customers about accessing dashboards online? Is this ever going to be operational? I am paying AWS monthly while waiting for a solution that seems farther away—is it time to give up?
Were you able to resolve the problem? I am encountering the same situation this January 2023.

[user_name], I started this discussion because I faced the same issue. The problem persists. [company_name] engineering in Germany was notified, but hasn't found a fix yet, so the case was sent to their Research and Development team. Hopefully they will address it, but after several months there’s been no update. I’ll share any news here as soon as I hear it. My last resort is to uninstall every version of [product_name] and related software, then do a clean install of [product_name] [version_no] and [version_no] SP1. I need to wait until February to test in the cloud due to AWS free tier limits—paying for something that doesn’t work is exhausting. Did you upgrade your software, or did you start from [version_no]?

[user_name], thanks for your response. I appreciate your efforts and am interested in updates from [company_name] and AWS. I know you’ll share new information here. Best regards from Mexico. For reference, I started with [product_name] [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]. I have no background with earlier modules or older software. Most of my projects using local web apps via SD card have succeeded, and I’ve run up to five [product_name] units on one LAN. Frustration began when trying AWS integration.

Hello [user_name], Hello [user_name], Personally, I do not favor putting critical system control on the Internet, nor do I trust storing data with a company that provides cloud services. Why not set up your own VPN server for direct, secure access to your systems? An Internet connection remains necessary, but with your own VPN you retain full control and avoid additional costs. Guides for setting up servers with Raspberry Pi, VM, or ProxMox are widely available online. Regards, [user_name] (translated with Google)

analysis.insight_summary: Several users are facing issues where, despite deploying their [product_name] projects to AWS and connecting their PLC devices, interactive controls are unresponsive and no data exchange happens. Various troubleshooting steps—including different AWS regions and software versions—have failed. Users are frustrated and worried about ongoing AWS expenses and delivering promised features to customers, causing concerns about workflow and reputation. Official support from [company_name] has not provided a solution, and the issue continues without resolution for multiple users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] projects to work reliably on AWS, providing fully responsive controls and consistent data exchange. They want assurance that offered features operate as advertised, allowing seamless remote customer access through the internet.
